page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.2xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 8 dedicated physical cores with single-thread execution. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Storage is a key highlight, featuring a bundled 5000 GB local NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory subsystem performance, with the Passmark memory score reaching the top tier and large-block read-only memory bandwidth registering at 189.45 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs strongly at 14.41 GB/sec. Most general compute benchmarks, including stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and static web serving throughput, fall within the average range. However, cryptographic performance is a notable tradeoff, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 25%, and medium-model LLM prompt processing performing in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i8ge.2xlarge offers high resource density, combining substantial NVMe storage capacity with a generous memory allocation per core on an ARM-based architecture. This profile makes it highly suitable for storage-intensive and database workloads, such as relational databases, NoSQL stores, caching layers like Redis, and data-intensive processing tasks that benefit from fast local storage and high memory bandwidth.
